name: Eyelid tape / fold stickers

lead: Eyelid tape and fold stickers are small, often crescent-shaped adhesive strips placed on the upper lid so the skin folds into a visible crease. People with single (monolid) lids use them for a double eyelid look without surgery, and looksmaxxers also use them to lift hooded or drooping lids.

The effect lasts as long as the strip stays on. Research is limited to a few small studies and reports: a 2020 study looked at the front surface of the eye after four weeks of wear in young women with single eyelids, a case series described tape holding up a drooping lid in myotonic dystrophy type 1, and a 2025 paper reviewed long-term use.

paras: The strip sticks to the lid skin and holds a fold above the lash line, imitating the crease a levator attachment forms naturally. It is applied daily, often under or alongside makeup, and removed at night. It is the non-surgical counterpart to double eyelid surgery.

Skin irritation from adhesives and repeated lid stretching are the concerns most often mentioned in the cosmetic and plastic surgery literature. Eyelid tape is a cosmetic product sold without prescription in most markets.

chain: Double eyelid or more open eye
angle.text: Eyelid tape and fold stickers create a temporary upper-lid crease, giving a double eyelid look or a more open eye straight away. They are removable and are the non-surgical counterpart to double eyelid surgery. Small studies have looked at effects on the eye surface after weeks of wear.

lead: Eyelid tape, also sold as fold stickers, crease tape or double eyelid tape, consists of thin adhesive strips applied to the upper eyelid to create a temporary crease. Pressing the lid skin into a fold above the lash line gives the look of a double eyelid: a larger-looking eye, more visible lid space and a more defined eye area. Many East Asians use the product for this purpose as a temporary means of increasing perceived beauty [1]. It is the non-surgical counterpart to double eyelid surgery, which creates a permanent crease in people who do not have one naturally [2].

In looksmaxxing communities the tape is discussed both as a way to simulate a double eyelid and as a stopgap for droopy or hooded lids, including mild ptosis [3]. The effect is fully reversible and lasts only while the strip stays on [4].

Published research includes a four-week wear study on ocular surface health [1], a case report describing the tape as an option for severe ptosis in myotonic dystrophy [5], and a 2025 clinical study of 267 outpatients in Aesthetic Plastic Surgery that examined eyelid laxity and surgical outcomes in people who used tape heavily [6].

paras: Eyelid tape is sold in rolls or as pre-cut strips, often in a thin crescent or sickle shape, that adhere to the skin of the upper lid. When the wearer opens the eye, the strip pushes the skin above it into a fold that resembles a natural supratarsal crease [1].

A double eyelid is an upper lid with a visible crease. Surveys summarised on Wikipedia report that the crease is naturally present in about 41% of Koreans and roughly 70 to 83% of Chinese and Japanese people [2]. Surgical creation of the crease is described as one of the most commonly performed cosmetic procedures in Taiwan and South Korea, and the first recorded operation is credited to Dr. Kotaro Mikamo in Japan in 1896 [2]. Tape and stickers are used by people who want the appearance without surgery.

Eyelid tape sits in a family of temporary crease products. Wikipedia describes eyelid glue, sold in Japan as 'Eye Putti', as a water-soluble adhesive first available in the late 1970s: it is painted on the upper lid, which is pushed up with a small plastic prong and held while the glue dries for about a minute, and it is also used by men [4]. A variant called eyelid tape or crease tape is a fibrous elastic strip trimmed to shape and placed on the lid; both wear off and need reapplying after a few hours, and glue may cause irritation [4].

Wikipedia lists circle contact lenses and East Asian blepharoplasty as related options with a similar visual aim [4]. Permanent double eyelid surgery has two main families: non-incisional suture ligation, which is quicker with faster recovery but gives a crease that may fade, and incisional techniques, which give a more durable crease but take longer to recover from [2]. Wikipedia reports it as the most common aesthetic surgery in Taiwan and widespread in South Korea [2].

Wikipedia notes that double eyelids are viewed as a sign of beauty in East Asia and that surgery aims to make the eyes look larger and more expressive. It presents two views of the history of the procedure: one holds that it was meant to westernise eyes, and the other that most Japanese women already had double eyelids and that Mikamo regarded single eyelids as monotonous and expressionless, so the operation enhanced a feature already valued locally [2][4].

On looksmax.org, eyelid tape appears in threads about drooping eyelids. One poster suggests tape as a fallback for "mild ptosis on random days" when other home measures they describe do not work, while acknowledging that they have no proof for their suggested routine [3].

Forum users in such threads tend to frame hooded or droopy lids as a lost opportunity for a more open, alert eye area, and tape as the cheapest reversible option. These are community views rather than published findings [3].

Strips are cut or pre-shaped to the lid, placed along the intended crease line, and the lid is opened so the skin folds over the edge. Wikipedia describes the related crease tape as a fibrous elastic strip trimmed to shape, and eyelid glue as a liquid painted on and set with a small prong; both wear off after a few hours and need reapplying [4]. Wearers also use them to even up lids that differ between the two eyes, or to lift hooded lids so makeup and the eye shape show more, which is how the product appears in looksmaxxing threads [3]. Some users go on to double eyelid surgery for a permanent crease, with non-incisional suture methods and incisional methods differing in recovery and durability [2].

The adhesive sits next to the eye and is pressed against the lid. In a 2020 study, 29 young women with single eyelids wore tape at least eight hours a day, five days a week, for four weeks. Researchers reported increases in conjunctival and corneal staining and in meibomian gland dysfunction, reductions in tear break-up time and intraocular pressure, and incomplete blinking in all participants by week 3, while participants' reported comfort did not change significantly. The authors advised patients and eye care practitioners to be aware of the potential implications of wear [1].

A 2025 hospital study in Aesthetic Plastic Surgery surveyed 267 outpatients (mean age about 24, almost all female). Nearly half reported using tape for one to two years, and most of those reported discomfort and a lasting change in eyelid shape. Vertical lid pull tests did not differ between users and non-users, but parallel lid pull results did. Asymmetry, numbness and hypertrophic scarring were recorded only in tape users who went on to surgery, and excised tissue showed differences in collagen and skin structure. The authors concluded that prolonged tape use may result in eyelid laxity that could make later blepharoplasty harder [6].

Wikipedia notes that glue products may cause skin irritation [4]. Medical tape is also used in other clinical contexts, such as taping eyelids closed during anaesthesia to protect the cornea [7]; that use is unrelated to cosmetic fold creation.

A 2020 study in the International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health recruited 29 young adult women with single eyelids and measured blinking, ocular surface health, tear break-up time, intraocular pressure and comfort weekly over four weeks of tape wear. Several surface measures worsened and blinking became incomplete, while self-reported comfort was unchanged [1].

A 2022 case report in the American Journal of Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation described a middle-aged man with myotonic dystrophy type 1 and severe ptosis for whom surgery was contraindicated. Double eyelid tape increased his palpebral fissure height and visual field and improved his functional score, and the authors proposed it as a therapeutic option for such patients [5].

A 2025 study in Aesthetic Plastic Surgery combined a survey of 267 outpatients, lid laxity testing, and a surgical comparison of 22 heavy tape users and 11 non-users who underwent double eyelid surgery, with histology of excised skin. Its authors reported associations between prolonged tape use and eyelid laxity [6]. No randomized trials of tape for appearance outcomes have been published.

lore.intro: Eyelid tape is discussed in looksmaxxing forums mainly as a cheap, reversible way to open up hooded or droopy lids [3].

timeline.event: Dr. Kotaro Mikamo performs the first recorded double eyelid surgery in Japan, the permanent counterpart to tape [2].
Eyelid glue ('Eye Putti') becomes available in Japan, the forerunner of tape and sticker products [4].
A four-week wear study examines anterior ocular health in young women with single eyelids [1].
Report describes tape as an option for severe ptosis in myotonic dystrophy type 1 [5].
Aesthetic Plastic Surgery article addresses long-term tape use [6].
Hospital cohort recruitment for the long-term tape study closes (January 2022 to January 2024) [6].
